title: The curve you draw over the bars

objectives.statement: State the two parameters that fix a normal distribution, compute the one, two and three standard deviation bands for a stated mean and standard deviation, and read a probability as an area between two values rather than a height at one.

Convert the empirical rule into predicted counts for a stated sample, compare those predictions against observed counts tail by tail as an informal diagnostic, and explain when a normal probability plot or calibrated procedure is needed before making a binary fit decision.

Compute a z-score for a measurement against a named reference distribution, explain why the score is unchanged by a unit conversion, and separate what a z-score reports as a distance from what only a distributional assumption can turn into a probability.
Select the binomial model for the number of yes-or-no results in a fixed set of trials, test its four conditions against a described study, and compute the expected count and its standard deviation.

scenes.title: The curve someone drew over the bars
Two numbers, and the whole curve is decided
One ruler for measurements that share no units
The same check, run on a population that fails it
When the question is a count, the curve is the wrong tool
Practice, with the props taken away one at a time
The same method, on a measurement that is not glucose
Clinical wrap-up: planning a clinic from a curve
